title: One-sided grid Sperner is PPADS-hard in the decision-tree world
claim: SINK (in a directed graph of in- and out-degree at most 1 with a standard source, find a sink; Beame et al.'s PPADS-complete problem) reduces to one-sided 2D Sperner on the side-m triangular grid with FLAT-STATES-20261107-001B's fixed boundary (find a fully labelled small triangle oriented like the boundary), with m = O(N^2) for N nodes and decision trees of depth O(log N). Every potential edge is drawn as a fixed rectilinear route; each crossing of two present routes is resolved by turning each incoming arm into the adjacent outgoing arm of the other, which keeps every in- and out-degree; each present path is a two-lane tube (colour 1 on the path, 2 on its right) on a background of 0, the standard source's tube entering through the boundary's door. Fully labelled triangles then occur exactly at tube ends: positively oriented at sinks, negatively at non-standard sources. Hence one-sided grid Sperner is PPADS^dt-complete, and the same construction makes two-sided grid Sperner PPAD^dt-complete.
failure_conditions: A fully labelled triangle away from a tube end, or one at a tube end with the wrong orientation.
A tube colour clashing with the fixed boundary, or a positive triangle that maps back to no SINK solution.
A colour depending on pointers other than those of edges drawn near it (the reduction would not be shallow).
A control (no uncrossing, turn radius 2, mirrored lanes) that the check fails to reject.
foundation_claim_scope: Every SINK instance (by the proof); checked on every pointer structure on 3 nodes with each single pointer change, and on random instances on 4..7 nodes.

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-11-07.
validation.status: by hand, with the construction checked exhaustively on 3 nodes and on random instances, a locality check and three negative controls; no human or external review
validation.novelty: known-with-delta: positive Sperner is PPADS-complete in dimension 3 and above (Beame-Cook-Edmonds-Impagliazzo-Pitassi 1998) and on surfaces of non-zero genus (Friedl-Ivanyos-Santha-Verhoeven 2006), and 2D Sperner is PPAD-complete (Chen-Deng 2006/2009). The delta: the planar one-sided case, because Chen-Deng's uncrossing keeps orientations, written for the decision-tree model with FLAT-STATES-20261107-001B's boundary.
